newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUDAPEST MILLING WHEAT PRICES RISE ON RAIN F'CAST.
newsitem.headline: BUDAPEST MILLING WHEAT PRICES RISE ON RAIN F'CAST.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued to rise on Wednesday on forecasts of rainy weather for the weekend, dealers said.
"The market has all eyes on the weather forecasts," said Robert Monostori of grains trading company Agrimpex.
Hungary's Meteorological Service (OMSZ) said it expected rains throughout the country from Friday or Saturday the latest.
"We expect rainfall across the country during the weekend, and at the moment it looks like there's going to be a lot," said Denes Torok of OMSZ.
Monostori said recent and expected rains could lower the quality of the grain crop with higher quality milling wheat expected to fall short of its usual 80 percent share of the total.
Farmers' union MOSZ, although maintaining its original forecast for this year's wheat crop, said earlier today that it also expected a lower quality wheat crop.
Official forecasts put this year's Hungarian wheat crop at around five million tonnes compared with last year's 3.9 million, but MOSZ's forecast was almsot 500,000 tonnes lower.
Prospects of wheat quailty problems led many traders to close selling positions, Monostori added.
Milling wheat prices rose for all maturities by between 190 forints and the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne.
August milling wheat closed at 21,270 forints, up 190, December rose 390 to 23,170 and May put on 380 forints to end at 25,480.
Monostori said that the movement of feed wheat prices was in line with expectations of a lower-quality crop as feed wheat remained steady or finished lower by between 140 and 150 forints.
He added, however, that if milling wheat prices continue to rise, feed wheat prices will have to follow sooner or later as otherwise feed wheat would become unpropoprtionally cheaper.
Elsewhere on the market, feed barley rose by between 250 and 400 forints in minimal turnover and little traded maize was steady or rose 60 to 200 forints.
Total grains turnover eased to 1,089 lots or 493.3 million forints from Tuesday's 1,320 lots or 594.5 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for the bulk of the turnover in volume terms with 756 lots.
